newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Koor first-quarter net off four percent.
newsitem.headline: Koor first-quarter net off four percent.

text.p: Koor Industries Ltd, Israel's largest holding company, said on Tuesday net profit fell four percent in the first quarter from a year earlier, to 205 million shekels ($60.3 million), or 13.5 shekels a share.

Koor attributed the decline to lower domestic sales, mainly in the telecommunications sector. Reduced orders from Bezeq Israel Telecom cut domestic telecommunications sales 56 percent from a year ago to $227 million.
Koor's return on equity was 5.73 percent, down from 6.84 percent a year earlier.

"The uncertainty in the political, security and economic environments has had a combined negative impact on the overall Israeli market and in particular on the building, infrastructure, telecommunication and tourism industries, which are on the verge of a crisis," Koor said in a statement.
The company saw group exports increase 19.7 percent in the quarter from a year earlier to $383 million, but the drop in local sales cut overall revenues 3.2 percent to 3.093 billion shekels.

In addition, Koor said, profitability on exports was lower than on domestic sales, mainly due to an overvalued Israeli currency. As a result, operating profit was down 26.7 percent from the year-earlier quarter.
Koor said any recovery of the domestic market would take time and therefore it would be focusing on export sales, despite lower margins.

"The erosion of profitability will continue as long as the Israeli government and the Bank of Israel do not implement measures that ensure a change in the (shekel) exchange rate," Koor said in a statement.

Koor's net earnings were lifted by 94 million shekels in capital gains from the sale of holdings in Israel Edible Products, Hanita Metal Works, Tadiran Information Systems and Q Multimedia during the quarter.

The company said it regarded the sale of holdings in its core businesses to strategic partners to be an integral part of its business. "Therefore, (they) should not be considered as a one-time and non-recurring effect," it said.
Koor's principal holdings include Tadiran Ltd, Telrad and Makhteshim Chemical Works Ltd.
